Gofo's new Dallas warehouse is twice the size of the previous facility, allowing it to process more parcels while improving efficiency. (Photo: Gofo) 

 Eric Kulisch August 27, 2026 7 min read

Parcel delivery startup Gofo has doubled the capacity of its Dallas processing center after moving into a new building and installing automated sortation equipment, as it races other regional carriers to build national scale. 

The larger terminal comes on line ahead of the peak season rush, allowing the company to absorb greater volume in the central United States rather than adding temporary facilities mid-season. Gofo says it expects parcel volume to jump 50% above normal weekly levels during the period between Thanksgiving and Christmas. 

Gofo inaugurated the new facility, which adds about 200,000 square feet of new space along with a large-scale double-deck cross-belt sorter, last week. The new site has 42 dock doors and can handle up to 45,000 parcels per hour, doubling daily capacity to 800,000 pieces per day, the company said in a news release on Tuesday.

# FST Logistics Expands Central Ohio Presence with New West Jefferson, Ohio Facility 

Dublin, OH – FST Logistics, a leading third-party logistics provider specializing in temperature-controlled transportation, retail consolidation, warehousing and supply chain solutions, is proud to announce the expansion of its Central Ohio footprint with the opening of a new facility in West Jefferson, Ohio. The new location adds 343,500 square feet of warehouse space to FST’s growing network and strengthens the company’s ability to support customers’ growth throughout the Midwest and beyond. 

The expansion provides additional capacity for FST to support the evolving needs of its customers, while creating opportunities to serve new customers seeking strategic warehousing and distribution solutions in Central Ohio. The facility features 38 dock doors, two drive-in doors, 40-foot clear height, 254 parking spaces and 85 trailer parking spaces, providing the infrastructure and capacity needed to support a wide range of customer operations.

# SEKO Logistics compounds U.S. growth, adding capacity across the Midwest and Texas 

SCHAUMBURG, Ill. — July 28, 2026 — SEKO Logistics (SEKO), the leader in end-to-end global logistics, is building on a sustained run of U.S. network investment with new and expanded facilities across the Midwest and Texas. The continued buildout deepens capacity across the network's core services — expedited ground solutions, international freight forwarding, white glove last mile delivery, contract logistics and customs brokerage — in markets where customer demand is concentrating, strengthening SEKO's ability to serve each region while extending the reach of its national and global accounts. The additions build on a U.S. footprint that now spans 64 locations, the largest and most expansive freight forwarding and 3PL network in the country.

- Large-scale logistics center equivalent to 14 soccer fields provides infrastructure to accommodate major customers and growing cargo volumes.
